title: Bodhrán
summary: The bodhrán is the Irish frame drum: a goatskin stretched over a wooden hoop, struck with a short double-ended stick called a tipper while the other hand presses the inside of the skin to change the pitch. It drives jigs and reels in Irish dance music with a lilting pulse of down and up strokes.
howToPlay: Five pads are five sounds: the down stroke, the lighter up stroke, a pressed note with the hand against the skin, a higher note struck near the rim, and a rim click.
Marks fall toward the line; strike the matching pad as each one lands.
The jig counts six eighth notes to a bar in two groups of three, the reel eight to a bar in four groups of two, and the slip jig nine in three groups of three.
rules: Every pulse is one eighth note for the jigs and the slip jig; for the reel a beat is a quarter note and the off beats fall halfway between.
A stroke within a short moment of the mark is perfect; a close one is good; extra strokes cost points.
Three stars need nearly every stroke on time.
heritageNote: The bodhrán entered Irish session music mainly in the 1960s, when players such as Seán Ó Riada brought it into ensembles, and its playing has since grown from a steady pulse into tonal, melodic patterns. It is played in sessions and bands across Ireland and in Irish communities worldwide.
credits: Instrument: Irish tradition; rhythms written for this game
